query: What reasons or compliance risks appear in declined expenses?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorising what was purchased gives a useful grouping axis for spotting patterns in declined expenses. Values are soundly read from short_description/ci, though the RAM-as-'miscellaneous' case is a slightly loose read.

per_column.name: asset_hardware_subtype
per_column.rationale: Refines hardware into subtypes, a legitimate additional axis. Mostly well grounded and NULL/Unknown correctly used for non-hardware. The 'RAM component' labelled 'peripheral_accessory' is a mild misclassification.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated entry could be relevant to compliance, but the basis is unclear from the provided fields; every sample is 'manually_entered' with no evident textual support, suggesting an inferred/invented distinction.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: A trivial null-check restating the existing source_id column; well grounded but adds little analytical leverage for the compliance query.

per_column.name: vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor extraction is a genuinely useful axis for compliance/spend analysis. Values track the source text well; 'ISP Services' → 'other_known' is defensible, 'generic_unnamed' correctly flags silent cases.

per_column.name: is_premium_or_luxury_item
per_column.rationale: A luxury flag is directly relevant to compliance risk, but it is near-constant (only 10 true) limiting leverage, and the criteria for 'premium' are only weakly supported by the text; samples are plausible.

per_column.name: is_travel_category_hardware_mismatch
per_column.rationale: A mismatch flag between category and item type is a targeted compliance-risk signal directly serving the query. Requires cross-field inference; sample values appear consistent, though correctness depends on the original category field not shown.

per_column.name: ci_name_quality
per_column.rationale: Data-quality of the ci label can plausibly correlate with declined/flagged entries, giving a modest new axis. Values are soundly derived from the ci string content.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine grouping axes (vendor, category, subtype, mismatch and luxury flags) that support investigating reasons and compliance risks in declined expenses, and their values are generally well grounded in short_description/ci. Weak spots: source_id_present is a trivial restatement of an existing field, and entry_origin appears inferred without clear textual support (all samples 'manually_entered'), the main groundedness concern. Occasional loose categorisations (RAM as miscellaneous/peripheral) are minor.
